title: Plain English
subtitle: No jargon. No small print. Just what it means
description: Plain English translates the confusing bits of life: contracts, bills, medical letters, tax forms and tech talk. It says what a thing means for you, what you need to do and by when, in words you’d use yourself.

sample.text: It means nothing is final yet. Either side can still walk away until contracts are signed. Don’t pay for anything non-refundable until then.
It’s a fixed daily fee for being connected, whether you use energy or not. You pay it on top of what you use. Yours is 60p a day, about £219 a year.
The yearly cost of borrowing, fees included. A 20% APR on £1,000 costs you about £200 over a year if you don’t pay it down.
I got a letter from HMRC
Tell me what it says. Mostly these ask for one of three things: a payment, a form or a check. Look for the date near the top. That’s your deadline.
what does this mean: “indemnify and hold harmless”?
You’re agreeing to cover their costs if something goes wrong because of you. It’s common, but ask whether it covers everything or only your own mistakes.
